use: Father as a role ('a father', 'his father'), not what you call him.
Mother as a role ('a mother', 'her mother'), not what you call her.

example.english: You look just like your mother.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo wa futari no ko no hahaoya desu
examplePolite.ja: 彼女は二人の子の母親です

example.english: Those two look like parent and child.

examplePolite.english: Parents and children can take part together.

notes: Oyakodon, chicken and egg on rice, is named after it.

example.english: I'm the eldest son, you know.

notes: Often carries family duties, like looking after the parents.
The second son and daughter are jinan and jijo.

use: Your own grandchild; someone else's is omagosan.

example.ja: 孫がかわいくてしょうがない
example.english: My grandkids are just too cute.

use: Your own grandfather in polite talk with outsiders; at home say ojiichan.

example.romaji: sofu ga kyonen nakunatta n da
example.ja: 祖父が去年亡くなったんだ
example.english: My grandfather passed away last year.

examplePolite.english: My grandfather is a retired teacher.

use: Your own grandmother in polite talk with outsiders; at home say obaachan.

example.romaji: sobo no ie wa inaka ni aru
example.ja: 祖母の家は田舎にある
example.english: My grandmother's house is in the countryside.

examplePolite.ja: 私は祖母に育てられました
examplePolite.english: I was raised by my grandmother.

use: Men's casual word for their own father; also any middle-aged man, or the owner of a small shop.

example.ja: 昨日親父とケンカした
example.english: I had a fight with my old man yesterday.

use: Homely, old-fashioned way to call your mother; also in rough men's talk.

example.ja: 母ちゃん、お腹すいたよ

use: Men's casual word for their own mother when talking to others.

example.romaji: ofukuro no ryouri ga ichiban da yo
example.ja: おふくろの料理が一番だよ

notes: Ofukuro no aji means home cooking like Mum makes.

use: Homely, old-fashioned way to call your father.

example.ja: 父ちゃん、早く帰ってきてね

use: Blunt word for an old man or your own grandpa; can sound rude.

example.ja: あのじいさん、また怒ってるよ
